summary: Discovery focused on data residency constraints for EU and US financial data, HIPAA adjacency questions, and logging/audit retention requirements. Customer weighing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; main concerns: log retention policy, KMS/HSM controls, network egress, and contract (BAA). Redwood AE+SE committed to docs and a Dedicated perf test.
topics: GDPR and EU data residency expectations (Schrems II implications)
HIPAA adjacency and BAAs for small user PII (financial + health-like attributes)
Log retention, redaction, and audit export controls
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs (latency/cost/compliance)
KMS/HSM integration and key custody options
transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey team, thanks for joining. We're here to understand Brighton's residency and logging constraints so we can map to Redwood's hosted/dedicated/private options.
[00:09] Jordan: Thanks Alex, yeah, quick agenda — I'm Jordan, Head of Data; Priya is our legal lead, Marcus runs infra. We have some EU funds and a handful of US-regulated accounts.
[00:20] Priya: Hi — our questions are mostly around how logs are handled, where data at rest lives, and whether we can get a BAA for anything PHI-adjacent.
[00:30] Samira: Great — I'll jump into the technical bits too. Quick clarifying q: when you say logs, do you mean application-level transcripts, system logs, or audit traces?
[00:38] Marcus: All of it. App transcripts for generating content (those are the big concern), plus any debug logs and traces. We need retention windows and ability to purge.
[00:47] Alex: Understood. Briefly, Hosted is our standard cloud API with regional tenancy and ISO/SOC compliance. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools — single-tenant — with stronger tenancy guarantees. Private is VPC/on-prem for full control.
[00:58] Jordan: For EU funds — EU-only residency is a hard ask for some clients because of Schrems II and customer contracts. Do you support EU-only encryption keys or customer-managed keys?
[01:08] Samira: Yes, we support KMS integrations; for Dedicated and Private you can bring your own KMS or HSM in a supported cloud region. Hosted supports CMKs in some regions depending on the contract — we'll confirm which regions.
[01:19] Priya: And for the Hosted option, if keys are managed by Redwood, where are they stored? Are they in the same region as the data?
[01:26] Samira: Currently keys are in the same cloud region for region-scoped deployments, but for multi-regional hosted we use central key management — that's why many customers on strict residency choose Dedicated or Private.
[01:36] Marcus: What about audit logs — can we export logs into our SIEM in real time? And are transcripts obfuscated automatically?
[01:44] Alex: We have log export hooks — S3/Cloud Storage and streaming to SIEM via syslog/Kinesis. For transcripts, we offer automatic redaction rules and token-level masking, but by default raw transcripts are retained according to the retention policy you select.
[01:57] Jordan: Retention policy — we need 7 years for certain records for a subset, 3 years for others. Can you set different retention windows per dataset or per route?
[02:06] Samira: Yes, retention can be configured per route/model in Dedicated and Private. Hosted has retention tiers but smaller granularity; we can set per-customer defaults, but per-route gets tricky unless you're on Dedicated/Private.
[02:18] Priya: HIPAA — we have users who might submit PHI in notes. We need a BAA and assurances about breach notification windows. Do you execute BAAs?
[02:27] Alex: We do execute BAAs for customers with the right plan and architecture (usually Dedicated or Private). For Hosted, we handle on a case-by-case basis; typically Dedicated or Private are recommended for HIPAA-level governance.
[02:37] Marcus: Network controls — can you restrict egress so the models only talk within our VPC or authorized endpoints?
[02:44] Samira: On Private, yes — full network control. Dedicated offers VPC peering and egress controls; Hosted is more limited but we can restrict region-level egress and use private link options in some clouds.
[02:56] Jordan: Any certifications? SOC 2 Type II? ISO 27001?
[03:01] Alex: We have SOC 2 and are in process for ISO 27001 renewal; will send artifacts. Customers ask for penetration test reports and we've got NDA-driven packages for those.
[03:11] Priya: On logs again — can you separate audit trails for admin actions vs model inputs? For compliance we need immutable audit trails for admin.
[03:19] Samira: Yes, admin audit trails are separate and we can increase WORM-style retention for those. Model inputs/transcripts are stored in the application logs bucket unless you choose to disable retention and only stream to your SIEM.
[03:33] Marcus: How does the KV cache interact with PII? If someone hits the same prompt, is there a risk of data from one customer appearing for another?
[03:41] Samira: KV cache is partitioned per-tenant; in Dedicated and Private it's single-tenant so no cross-tenant bleed. Hosted uses tenant-scoped caches — cross-tenant shouldn't happen, but we recommend Dedicated for absolute isolation.
[03:53] Jordan: Ok. For EU clients we also have cross-border transfer clauses — can Redwood guarantee data never leaves EU for EU-flagged accounts?
[04:01] Alex: For Private deployed in an EU region or Dedicated capacity pinned to EU hardware, yes. Hosted can be region-scoped but sometimes redundancy means cross-region backups; we'll surface the exact replication behavior for the EU regions.
[04:12] Priya: About logging granularity: are user identifiers hashed? Are there pseudonymization features you support out-of-the-box?
[04:20] Samira: We offer built-in pseudonymization and hashing pipelines; you can choose to hash IDs on ingest, apply regex redaction, or post-process logs before retention. Some of those are configuration flags in Dedicated/Private; Hosted supports a subset.
[04:33] Marcus: Encryption at rest — AES-256? Are we able to use our own CMK so that revoking the key effectively prevents decryption?
[04:41] Samira: Yes AES-256 for encryption. With BYOK (bring-your-own-key) we can integrate with your cloud KMS/HSM such that key rotation/revocation is under your control for Dedicated and Private. Hosted has limited BYOK in certain regions.
[04:54] Jordan: Any chance we can get a short architecture diagram showing how logs and keys flow for each deployment mode?
[05:00] Alex: Absolutely — we'll attach an architecture deck.
[05:03] Priya: For auditing, do you provide signed audit logs or tamper-evident logs? We need evidence that audit trails haven't been altered.
[05:11] Samira: We can enable append-only signed logs with cryptographic hashes and periodic checkpoints for Dedicated/Private. Hosted has retained audit trails but not the full append-only checkpoints unless part of an add-on.
[05:23] Jordan: Pricing question — any uplift for Dedicated with EU-only pins?
[05:28] Alex: Yes Dedicated has a premium because of reserved hardware and capacity guarantees; EU-only pinned pools add some geography premium. We'll send a pricing estimate.
[05:36] Marcus: For the Dedicated perf test, what duration do you recommend and what metrics will you capture?
[05:42] Samira: We usually run a 24-72 hour soak with synthetic traffic matching your latency and sequence length distribution, capturing p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and cost-per-token estimates. Also we'll run failure/failover tests if you want.
[05:55] Jordan: Internal stakeholders — legal & compliance will need the BAA and SOC artifacts; platform team wants the architecture doc and performance test.
[06:03] Alex: Great recap. Will also include a brief checklist for migration to Dedicated/Private and sample contract language for data residency.
[06:10] Priya: One last: incident response — time to notify, do you commit to 72-hour notification for breaches?
[06:17] Alex: Standard is 72 hours for incident notification; we'll align the exact SLA in the contract.
[06:22] Jordan: Perfect. Thanks — that's helpful.
[06:26] Alex: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the deck, SOC2, BAA draft, and schedule the perf test.
[06:33] [END]
